messages:
Nora (customer): Hey team — hitting JSON.parse errors from the API when I enable json_mode/structured output. Example response we got: {\"items\":[{\"id\":1, \"name\":\"foo\",}, {\"id\":2, \"name\":\"bar\"\n}]} — trailing comma and an unescaped newline. Client throws on parse.

Ava (support): Sorry about that, we can help. Can you paste the raw response + the request payload (including model/version and params)? Also are you using any of the structured_output helpers or a schema param?

Nora (customer): Minimal repro below. model: open-instruct-1.3, temp=0.0, json_mode=strict, prompt: 
```
Prompt: "Return items as a JSON array of objects with id:number and name:string. No extra text."
```
Request payload: {\"model\":\"open-instruct-1.3\",\"temperature\":0.0,\"json_mode\":\"strict\",\"prompt\":\"...\"}
Raw response we received: 
```
{\"items\":[{\"id\":1, \"name\":\"foo\",}, {\"id\":2, \"name\":\"bar\n\"}]}
```
Client error: JSON.parse throws at char 23.

Ava (support): Thanks. Two threads here: 1) possible model/schema drift producing trailing commas/newlines, 2) retries/backoff causing billing/latency. We'll collect request id/org id and escalate. @Marco / @Priya any immediate mitigation? :thinking:

Marco (eng): This is pretty common when generation isn't tightly constrained. Quick pragmatic fixes: server-side sanitizer + re-ask. Example regex to strip trailing commas before closing arrays/objects: 
```python
import re
clean = re.sub(r',(?=\\s*[\\]}])', '', raw_text)
```
Also a re-ask pattern: send the invalid output back with a repair prompt: 
```
"The JSON below is invalid. Correct it and return only valid JSON that conforms to the schema. Do not add commentary."
<INVALID_JSON>
```
Set temperature=0 and small max_tokens.

Priya (ml): Regex is fine short-term but brittle. Best pattern: 1) validate against the JSON schema using a library (jsonschema), 2) if invalid, prepare a concise repair prompt that includes the schema and the invalid output, 3) re-ask up to N times with exponential backoff (e.g., 1s, 2s, 4s) and abort to fallback after ~2-3 attempts. Example repair prompt: 
```
"You are a JSON validator. Fix the following JSON to match this schema: <SCHEMA>. Return only the corrected JSON.
Invalid: <INVALID_JSON>"
```
That reduces hallucinated repairs.

Ava (support): Also note retries = more tokens -> potential billing spike. Nora, can you share request_id/org_id + whether your client is auto-retrying? We saw a small edge 500 around the same time which increased latency and triggered client-side retries.

Nora (customer): Request id: req_3b9f1a, org: org-0c2b. Client had auto-retry enabled (3 tries) with no backoff. We patched client to disable retries for JSON-mode and added pre-parse sanitizer. Latency: single request sometimes jumped to 2.4s.

DeployBot: runtime:unified-json-policies v2 deployed to canary at 1765123600 — adds stricter output trimming and logs invalid-json events.

Marco (eng): On our side we'll add a targeted runtime post-processor that tries a minimal two-step self-heal: 1) apply lightweight cleanup (regex to remove trailing commas/newline fixes) 2) if still invalid, send a repair prompt to the same model with temp=0 and return repaired JSON. We'll default to max 2 internal repair attempts to limit token burn.

Priya (ml): For longer term: add schema-guided decoding signals (we're testing a constrained decoding mode) plus better model selection for structured outputs. In the meantime, recommend schema validation + repair-reask with backoff and a token cap.

Ava (support): Escalating to ml-infra and billing ops. Ticket INC-9832 created, attaching the repro and req_3b9f1a. We'll follow up within 24hrs with logs and mitigation.

Nora (customer): Thanks — short-term workaround worked: client-side strip trailing commas before parse + disabled auto-retries. That stopped the crashes. Appreciate the quick help. :thumbsup:

Marco (eng): FYI for others: if you use server-side re-ask, include the original prompt in the repair request so you maintain context and avoid losing required fields. Also prefer validation-first (don't blindly trust regex).

Ava (support): Closing loop: we'll monitor canary for invalid-json events and post an update in #eng-runtime. If you see regressions, drop the req id here.

Nora (customer): Will do — thanks everyone.
